result.lens: Python int() grammar for --a --b --d --f --g (integer-literal parser attack)

divergences.portOutput:
exit=2
stdout=""
stderr="usage: test17_executable [-h] --a A --b B --c C --d D --e E --f F --g G\ntest17_executable: error: argument --a: expected one argument\n"
divergences.explanation:
argparse's _negative_number_matcher is a Python regex `^-\d+$|^-\d*\.\d+$`, and Python's `$` matches at end of string OR immediately before a single trailing newline. So CPython classifies '-0
' as a negative-number VALUE, feeds it to int() (which strips the trailing whitespace) and succeeds. /output/lib/argparse/parser.mjs:17 uses `const NEGATIVE_NUMBER = /^-[\p{Nd}]+$|^-[\p{Nd}]*\.[\p{Nd}]+$/u`; JS `$` (no /m) only matches at the very end, so the token falls through to the unknown-option branch, is marked isOption=true, and --a reports 'expected one argument'. Fix: allow an optional single trailing 
 before each `$`. STILL REPRODUCIBLE. Affects every int option and every negative-number shape: ['--b','-0
',...], ['--d','-0
',...], ['--f','-0
',...], ['--g','-0
',...] all give exit 0 in ref vs exit 2 in port; ['--a','-1
',...] and ['--a','-12
',...] give ref exit 1 (construct FormatFieldError "given value -1" / "-12") vs port exit 2 'expected one argument'; ['--a','-1.2
',...] and ['--a','-.5
',...] give ref exit 2 "invalid int value: '-1.2\n'" vs port exit 2 'expected one argument'; non-ASCII digits behave the same because Python \d is Nd-aware: ['--a','-٠
',...], ['--a','-０
',...], ['--a','-𝟢
',...] all exit 0 in ref, exit 2 in port. Control: '--a=-0
' (explicit `=` form, which bypasses the matcher) matches, confirming the defect is exactly the regex anchor.

divergences.explanation: Unicode-version skew on the int()-rejection repr path. The frozen build is CPython 3.12 => UCD 15.0.0; the port's isPyPrintable in /output/lib/python/unicode.mjs tests /[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}\p{Cs}\p{Co}\p{Cn}\p{Zl}\p{Zp}\p{Zs}]/u against Node 18.19.1 / ICU 74.2 => UCD 15.1.0. Codepoints assigned in 15.1 but unassigned (Cn) in 15.0 are non-printable for Python's repr (\uXXXX / \UXXXXXXXX escape) but printable for the port (emitted raw). Exact divergent set, boundaries confirmed: U+2FFC..U+2FFF (IDC additions; U+2FFB matches) and U+2EBF0..U+2EE5D (CJK Ext I; U+2EBEF and U+2EE5E match) = 626 codepoints. Verified by random sampling across all planes: every failure landed in those ranges (e.g. U+2EC00, U+2ED40, U+2EE00). Reachable directly from the int() error path with a bare non-digit char, e.g. ['--a','⿼',...] -> ref "invalid int value: '\\u2ffc'" vs port "invalid int value: '⿼'"; ['--a','\U0002ebf0',...] -> ref "'\\U0002ebf0'" vs port raw f0 ae af b0. STILL REPRODUCIBLE. Fix: hard-code the UCD 15.0 unassigned ranges (or subtract the 15.1 additions) instead of relying on the host \p{Cn}.

divergences.explanation: sys.int_info.default_max_str_digits: CPython 3.11+ raises ValueError from int(str) when the literal has more than 4300 digit characters, so argparse turns it into a usage error; the port parsed it into a BigInt and failed later inside construct. Boundary probed exactly: 4300 digits accepted, 4301 rejected; underscores, sign and whitespace do NOT count toward the limit ('1'*2150+'_'+'1'*2150 = 4300 digits is accepted, '  '+'1'*4301+'  ' and '+'+'1'*4301 are rejected); leading zeros DO count ('0'*4301 and '0'*4300+'1' are rejected even though '0'*4299+'1' is accepted); non-ASCII digits count ('١'*4301 and '۱'*4301 rejected). NOTE: while this sweep was running, /output/lib/python/int.mjs was edited by another agent to add `const MAX_STR_DIGITS = 4300`, and all 10 boundary cases now match, so this divergence is no longer reproducible in the current tree - reported so it is kept as a regression test.

notes: Exhaustive Nd sweep: all 680 codepoints matched by \p{Nd} in Node 18/ICU 74.2 were tested one at a time as the whole --a value; 680/680 identical (digit VALUE verified, since format1 == a). No mismatch, so decimalDigitValue's run-scan heuristic is value-correct for every Nd codepoint.

Structural check of the run-scan heuristic: 680 Nd codepoints form 64 maximal contiguous runs, every run length is a multiple of 10, and only U+1D7CE..U+1D7FF (the 50 mathematical digits, 5 adjacent blocks) is longer than 10. So `(cp - runStart) % 10` is sound for UCD 15.1; it is a latent fragility only if a future UCD adds a non-10-aligned Nd run.

Non-Nd numerics: all 1151 \p{No} + \p{Nl} codepoints (superscripts, fractions, Roman numerals, circled digits, U+3007, U+1010x Aegean, U+0BF0 etc.) tested as --a; 1151/1151 identical - all rejected with byte-identical repr in the error message.

Whitespace: 93 candidate separator/control codepoints (all of U+0001-U+001F, U+007F, every \p{Zs}/\p{Zl}/\p{Zp}/\p{Cc}, plus U+00AD U+061C U+180E U+200B U+200C U+200D U+2060 U+2061 U+FEFF U+E0020) x 9 shapes (bare, leading, trailing, both, before sign, after sign, after minus, doubled, infix) = 837 cases; 837/837 identical. This confirms the port's hybrid model: U+0085/U+00A0/U+1680/U+2000-200A/U+2028/U+2029/U+202F/U+205F/U+3000 pad fine, while ASCII U+001C-U+001F, U+FEFF and U+200B are rejected. U+0000 cannot be tested (execve forbids NUL in argv).

Grammar shapes: 101 hand-built literals covering '', ' ', bare '+'/'-', '++1', '--1', '+-1', '-+1', '1+', '1-', underscores in every legal and illegal position ('_', '_1', '1_', '__1', '1__2', '1_2_3', '_1_', '1_2_', '0__0', '1_000_000'), leading zeros, 2**63-1/2**63/2**64-1/2**64/2**128 boundaries, 50- and 60-digit values, non-int forms ('1e3','0x10','0b101','0o17','1.0','.5','5.','inf','nan','None','True'), fullwidth/Arabic-Indic/Extended-Arabic-Indic/Devanagari/Bengali/Thai/Khmer/Mongolian/mathematical-bold/Nag-Mundari/segmented digits, mixed-script strings, and BOM/ZWSP/LRM/RLM/word-joiner padding. All matched except the >4300-digit cases.

Random mixed-script fuzz: 260 literals assembled from random digits drawn from all 68 ten-codepoint Nd blocks (1-3 digits, random underscore grouping, random sign, random ASCII/Unicode whitespace padding); 260/260 identical.

Printability/repr fuzz: 200 groups of 25 random codepoints from the full 0..0x10FFFF range plus 10 boundary probes; 202/210 matched and all 8 failures bisected into U+2FFC..U+2FFF / U+2EBF0..U+2EE5D (divergence 2). No other printability disagreement found.

Environment facts pinned: frozen build is libpython3.12 (UCD 15.0.0); the port runs on Node v18.19.1 with ICU 74.2 (UCD 15.1.0). UCD 15.1 added no new Nd, which is why the version skew shows up only in repr printability and not in the digit grammar.

Probe scripts (all under /tmp, none under /output): /tmp/par.mjs (parallel pair runner, PID-normalising), /tmp/nd.mjs, /tmp/nd2.mjs, /tmp/nn.mjs, /tmp/ws.mjs, /tmp/gram.mjs, /tmp/fuzz.mjs, /tmp/misc.mjs, /tmp/limit.mjs, /tmp/printab.mjs, /tmp/u151.mjs.

Relevant port files: /output/lib/argparse/parser.mjs (line 17, NEGATIVE_NUMBER), /output/lib/python/unicode.mjs (NON_PRINTABLE regex / isPyPrintable), /output/lib/python/int.mjs (pyInt, MAX_STR_DIGITS).
